documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.stance_why: The article sets no rule on student or instructor AI use. It says 'While these policy documents are in development' and defers to a steering committee that will 'define guidelines and policies', so it takes no stance and leaves the decision to future guidance.
documents.summary: An ITS FAQ saying ISU is forming an AI Steering Committee and that policies are still in development. It notes Gemini for Education is enabled on all ISU Google accounts and asks departments not to buy their own AI licenses because of data and security risks. It sets no teaching or academic-integrity rule.

units.why: The passage says ISU is 'forming an AI Steering Committee to define guidelines and policies', stating the institution-level purpose and process for AI governance; P56 (institution-wide framework) fits better than P54 because it sets aim and scope rather than promising revision.
units.anchor: ISU is forming an AI Steering Committee to define guidelines and policies
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P56, admin, informs. Phase differed: A general, B before-course. The sentence announces a committee to define institution-wide guidelines, which is a statement of purpose and scope rather than course or policy design for a course, so general.

units.why: 'While these policy documents are in development' says the policy is provisional and unfinished; this is P54 rather than P56 because the point is that the rules are not yet final.

units.why: 'Please refrain from purchasing individual AI licenses for your departments' asks departments not to buy their own AI tools; this steers toward vetted tools (P50), not equity of access (P51), and binds departments (admin).

units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code. Source: 'Please refrain from purchasing individual AI licenses for your departments' is a request to departments, so admin, should-not, P50.

units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type, phase and modality. Actor differed: A all, B admin. The sentence answers a departmental purchasing question and justifies the request to departments, so admin. Source: 'can expose student or institutional data and introduce security risks to ISU networks'.

units.why: The passage says generative AI use must honor 'existing commitments to security and privacy' and ISU values, and lists confidentiality, PII and academic integrity as concerns under consideration; this states principles for responsible AI use (P56) with no specific rule.
units.anchor: use of generative AI honors our existing commitments to security and privacy
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P56, general, informs. Actor differed: A admin, B all. The sentence states ISU's own commitment ('ISU also recognizes the necessity of ensuring...'), so the institution (admin) is the actor. A's frag_end spanned the next sentence, which is coded as a separate unit, so frag_end is narrowed to the end of this sentence as B had it.

units.why: The sentence lists issues 'being considered by the AI steering committee' (confidentiality, PII, academic integrity). It shows the policy is still being worked out, so P54 fits; the issue list is not itself a rule.
units.anchor: Concerns about confidentiality, protecting personally identifiable information (PII), academic integrity, and more are being considered
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this sentence separately; A folded it into the previous unit's fragment. Source: 'Concerns about confidentiality, protecting personally identifiable information (PII), academic integrity, and more are being considered by the AI steering committee.' It is a real statement that policy is still being worked out, so kept as P54, over-time, informs, admin.

notes: Only one included document (ITS FAQ); it is not a teaching policy. Official ISU General Counsel and Academic Integrity Center pages returned 403 and were not coded. Stance 'delegates' is a closest fit: the decision is deferred to a steering committee, not to instructors. Reconciled: 6 matched units, 1 kept from B only. Topic codes limited to the starter codebook.
